To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a strategy that is provably optimal for the case of no arrivals of queries is also optimal for the case with arrivals, (2) a strategy that sends a single copy of each query and aborts copies of answered queries is also optimal in the case with arrivals.

the optimal strategy in the case where queries arrive with a given probability, is to send a single copy of a query to the best information agent, and that the optimal strategy for the case where no queries arrive, is to send copies of queries to all information agents, and abort copies of answered queries.

“In a simple cooperative MAS, a provably optimal static strategy for querying information agents exists, and it performs well in a dynamic environment with queries arriving with a certain probability.”

the design of efficient strategies for querying information agents, in the context of a simple cooperative multi-agent system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal strategy for the problem is to send queries to the information agents in a round-robin manner, and that this strategy can be used even in the presence of query arrivals.
the strategy that sends only one copy of each query and does not abort answered copies is provably optimal, and performs very well in practice.

, when a collection of information agents is used for querying purposes by a set of querying agents, the optimal strategy for a querying agent is to send one copy of a query to the information agent with the highest expected answer time, and to abort the copy as soon as it receives an answer.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, when the querying agents are homogeneous (in terms of the queries they send, their arrival rates, etc.), the optimal strategy is to always use a single copy of each query, and never abort copies of answered queries.
a simple strategy can perform well even when the arrival rate of queries is not known a priori.
a strategy that is optimal in the static case is also good for the dynamic case with query arrivals, even when the query arrivals are not independent.
